title: Types and Programming Languages
why: The canonical textbook for chapter 7 typing rules, progress and preservation, subtyping and variance, and for chapter 8's Hindley-Milner reconstruction and Algorithm W (ch. 22-23).

title: Principal type-schemes for functional programs
why: The original paper defining Damas-Milner let-polymorphism and Algorithm W, the primary source for chapter 8's inference rules.

title: Generics implementation - GC Shape Stenciling
why: The Go team's own design explaining GC-shape stenciling plus dictionaries, why Go sits between full monomorphization and type erasure, and the itab/dictionary mechanics for chapter 9.

title: Efficiently Computing Static Single Assignment Form and the Control Dependence Graph
why: The original SSA paper defining dominance frontiers, minimal phi placement and renaming, and the dominance/dataflow framework for chapters 11 and 12.

title: Simple and Efficient Construction of Static Single Assignment Form
why: Presents the on-the-fly SSA construction algorithm that lowers an AST or bytecode directly to SSA without computing dominance frontiers, for chapter 12's alternative to Cytron.

title: LLVM Language Reference Manual
why: The authoritative spec of LLVM IR's SSA values, phi nodes, basic blocks and module structure, the reference for chapters 10 and 13.

title: Introduction to the Go compiler's SSA backend (cmd/compile/internal/ssa/README.md)
why: The Go compiler's own walkthrough of values, memory state, blocks/CFGs, the pass pipeline, rewrite rules, lowering and GOSSAFUNC, for chapters 10, 11 and 13.

title: Land ahoy: leaving the Sea of Nodes
why: V8 engineers explain what a Sea of Nodes IR is, why Turbofan used it, and why they replaced it with a CFG-based IR, the builder's write-up for chapter 13.
